Confirming an order now books a shipment through `CarrierGateway` and stores the tracking number on the order. The full test suite passes.

- **`Order`** has a nullable `trackingNumber` with an `assignTrackingNumber` setter.
- **`OrderService`** takes a `CarrierGateway`. `confirm` calls `carrier.book(orderId)` first, then stores the tracking number and sets `CONFIRMED`. If the carrier call throws, the order stays `PLACED` with no tracking number.
- **`OrderSummary`** has a new trailing `trackingNumber()` component. It is `null` until the order is confirmed.
- **`OrderServiceTest`** is new. It uses a fake gateway to check that confirm stores the tracking number and that a failed booking leaves the order unconfirmed.

Two things to be aware of:
- Confirming an order twice books two shipments. I didn't add a guard because it changes behaviour (throw or no-op), so that choice is yours.
- Nothing exercises the real `HttpCarrierGateway`. It still points at `https://carrier.example/api`, and the tests use a fake.
